..
Issued at 302 PM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

Pattern Synopsis: Broad long wave trough in place across western/ 
central North America; stronger short wave trough/PV anomaly over 
northwest Ontario with another digging southeast across the Prairie 
provinces.  Water vapor imagery also shows a weaker short wave 
trough crossing the Dakotas.  Weak upper low over the lower 
Mississippi/Tennessee River Valleys.  Positive tilt/-PNA trough over 
the Pacific Northwest and adjacent Pacific Ocean...trying to pick up 
an old cut off low northeast of Hawaii and pull it back into the 
"PV reservoir" so to speak.  This attempt looks like it will be 
unsuccessful...but the remnants of the Pacific Northwest short wave 
trough will feature prominently in Great Lakes weather during the 
first half of the coming week.  Strong -EPO ridge south of Alaska 
(+3 sigma 500mb height anomaly) poking northeast into the Canadian 
Territories. Narrow axis of 1.25-1.50 inch precipitable water values 
and steeper mid level lapse rates extends from the upper Lakes 
southwest into the Central Plains ahead of cold front...with 
cold/dry air advection behind it across the northern Plains/upper 
Midwest.     

Primary Forecast Concerns: 

Cold front passage late this afternoon/evening: Cold front at 1800Z 
ran from a MQT-GRB-DBQ line...with a pre-frontal wind shift moving 
into Lake Michigan.  Water vapor imagery shows upward motion field 
with short wave trough north of Lake Superior spreading across Upper 
Michigan and toward Lake Michigan.  Getting an increase in cloud 
streets bubbling up across Lower Michigan...with a few hundred J/kg 
of MLCAPE west of the I-75 corridor along with decreasing CINH.  So 
expect the threat for scattered showers/thunderstorms to continue 
until the cold front and short wave trough depart the area this 
evening.   Narrow band of post-frontal St/Sc will give way to some 
lake induced Sc overnight as 925mb temperatures sink below +12C.  

Cooler/breezy with shower chances Sunday: Next short wave trough in 
the series...digging southeast out of the Canadian Prairies this 
afternoon...will swing across the upper Lakes Sunday.  850mb 
temperatures dropping below 4C across Lake Superior will result in a 
decent amount of lake-induced instability.  Combined with larger 
scale forcing/moisture will likely get showers going off Lake 
Superior Sunday morning.  For now expect rain chances will be lower 
south of the Straits Sunday afternoon...won't rule it out given the 
strength of the forcing but the instability/moisture profiles across 
northern Lower not as impressive.  Wondering how much of the lake 
component will linger into Sunday evening.  High temperatures in the 
70s and lower 80s this afternoon will give way to highs mainly in 
the 60s for Sunday (with highs 70-75 across far southeast portion of 
the forecast area closer to Saginaw Bay).  Winds also expected to be 
gusty with mixing during the day...west/northwest gusts 20 to 30 mph 
anticipated.

Dry Monday with more substantial rain threat Monday night/Tuesday 
(and possibly beyond but much uncertainty regarding that):  High 
pressure centered over Michigan Monday gives way to deep layer 
southwest flow Monday evening...low level jet directed into the 
upper Lakes with precipitable water values at or above 1.75 inches. 
Main focus Monday night will be across Upper/northwest Lower 
Michigan...then shifting into central and northeast Lower as the day 
progresses Tuesday.  Trends continue to suggest drying across Upper 
Michigan during the afternoon Tuesday...remains to be seen how 
aggressively this pushes into northern Lower (more on that below). 
Highest probabilities exceeding 1 inch rainfall/24 hours ending 
0000Z Wednesday remain across eastern Upper and the Tip of the Mitt 
counties.  Probably some much needed rain across eastern Upper where 
things have been quite dry over the past two weeks (less than 25 
percent normal precipitation) with some spots of D1 (moderate) 
drought showing up. 

Evolution beyond Tuesday afternoon is rather interesting...with an 
upper anticyclone become established over the southeastern U.S. 
Monday...and then expanding north with 594dam 500mb heights knocking 
on the door of southern Lower Tuesday.  This will set up a 
baroclinic zone across the upper Lakes during midweek...a 
synoptically ideal setup for a corridor of heavier rain potential. 
Exactly where this sets up will determine if our southern zones get 
clipped by this.  For now the forecast is dry for Wednesday...with 
rain returning Thursday.  There are some very small probabilities of 
>2 inches of rain Wednesday night/Thursday south of M-32.  So 
something to keep an eye on going forward.
